title: Canonical finite derived pullback tensor comparison
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1}$ for $n\geq0$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the finite derived pullback and tensor functors of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Define their canonical comparison $\mu_{f,n}:L f_n^*(M\otimes^L N)\simeq L f_n^*M\otimes^L L f_n^*N$ for arbitrary ambient derived objects $M,N$ by totalizing the ordinary module pullback/tensor isomorphism on flat-term K-flat representatives, descending to the derived category, and conjugating by the specified intrinsic realization and tensor-model isomorphisms. It is the actual map characterized by this representative square. Define the derived Koszul symmetry by descent of the signed cochain exchange $x_p\otimes y_q\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y_q\otimes x_p$. Include the four pullback/tensor comparison-family types for the coefficient categories and operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. These constructions introduce no alternative derived tensor or pullback functor. The canonical finite family satisfies the naturality, associativity, signed symmetry, both unit and pullback-composition equations with the recorded canonical operation comparisons.

source.place: Lemma 21.18.4 (Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product), for the morphism of ringed topoi (X_proet, (A_{E,n})_X) -> (Y_proet, (A_{E,n})_Y); the integral, rational and Qlbar levels follow the level-by-level definitions of the operations in def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom

proof.text: The existing coefficient comparison types, unit-normalized finite realization, tensor-model restriction, signed total symmetry and its derived descent are re-exported from the construction and braiding layers. canonicalFinitePullbackTensor is a definitionally identical API alias of finitePullbackTensorConstruction.

For signed braiding, form two natural transformations from tensor_Y followed by finite pullback to the swapped tensor of the pullbacks, using finitePullbackTensorConstructionIso and the two signed braidings. They agree on the localized flat K-flat pairs by lem-pur-finite-pullback-tensor-signed-representatives. For an arbitrary derived object choose a cochain preimage under Q and a flat K-flat resolution; its quasi-isomorphism gives an isomorphism to the original object. Naturality of the two transformations along the product of these isomorphisms, followed by cancellation of its invertible image, proves equality for every derived pair.

For composition, form two natural transformations from tensor followed by pullback along the composite to tensor of the two iterated pullbacks, using the natural canonical comparison isomorphisms and the specified pullback compositor. They agree on flat K-flat pairs by lem-pur-finite-pullback-tensor-composition-representatives. Resolve both inputs, use naturality along the product of the resolving isomorphisms, and cancel its invertible image to extend equality to every pair.

Form the two associativity paths as natural transformations from left-associated triple tensor followed by finite pullback to right-associated tensor of the three pullbacks. They agree on localized flat K-flat triples by the representative associativity calculation. Resolve all three inputs using finiteTensor_flat_representatives. Naturality along the product of the three resolving isomorphisms and cancellation of its invertible image give equality on every derived triple. Take the component and unfold only the canonical comparison alias.

Choose the single unit isomorphism supplied by the representative unit existence theorem. Each unit-equation path is a natural transformation: tensor-comparison naturality, tensor interchange and unitor naturality prove this in Lean. Resolve an arbitrary derived input and cancel the invertible source map to extend both equations from representatives. For uniqueness evaluate the right-unit equation at the source tensor unit, cancel the comparison and right unitor, and conjugate the resulting equality id tensor epsilon=id tensor epsilon-prime by the chosen unit isomorphism. Left-unitor naturality and cancellation give epsilon=epsilon-prime. Thus neither arbitrary-input unit coherence nor uniqueness is assumed by the new representative theorem.

proof_origin.place: Tags 07A4 and 03EL. D2 extends associativity and both unit equations from flat K-flat representatives by naturality and resolving isomorphisms, and proves unit uniqueness by tensor/unitor cancellation. Existing composition and signed-braiding proofs retained.
